newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FORECAST-WMC year net seen up 14 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FORECAST-WMC year net seen up 14 pct.

text.p: Higher output and stronger realised prices for nickel, alumina and copper are expected to have lifted WMC Ltd's net profit for the year to June 30 by 14 percent above that of the previous year, analysts said.
Analysts' average forecast for WMC's equity-accounted net profit before abnormals was A$401 million, compared with A$351.6 million in fiscal 1994/95.
Forecasts for WMC's profit, due next Thursday, ranged from A$383 million to A$425 million.

"There's higher nickel-in-concentrate production, higher refined copper production and higher equity share of alumina production and ... there were higher realised prices for alumina and for nickel," ANZ Securities analyst Rob Craigie noted.
Craigie forecast WMC's net profit at A$408 million.
However, WMC's profit figure might have been higher but for an appreciation in the Australia dollar which eroded offshore earnings.

WMC enjoyed a rise in nickel's average price over fiscal 1995/96 to about US$3.73 a pound from US$3.38 a year ago but this was somewhat mitigated by a two to three cent rise in the Australian dollar, analysts said.
Gold earnings also were hit by the halving of production at WMC's St Ives mine in Western Australia for about eight weeks in late 1995 when cracks were found in the mine's SAG mill.
"They then recovered that in the second half but they had to carry some additional costs," said BZW Australia analyst John MacKinnon, who pegged his full-year profit expectation at A$390 million.

WMC's Alcoa World Alumina joint venture with Aluminum Co of America would be the largest single contributor to WMC's bottom line in fiscal 1995/96 with total alumina production more than doubling to 10.1 million tonnes, analysts said.
"Certainly on alumina contracts, Alcoa ... realised a higher average percentage of the LME aluminium price in 1996 compared to '95," ANZ's Craigie said.
Copper profit contributions were seen up on the back of higher copper prices and higher copper production at the Olympic Dam and Nifty mines in South Australia.
"It shows the effect of the second optimisation (at Olympic Dam) that was completed the the end of the '94/95 year," Craigie said.
Uranium earnings also were expected to rise.
A slide in petroleum production due to Cyclone Olivia was seen offset by stronger oil prices to leave earnings flat to slightly higher for the year.
"Oil and gas will probably be a bit better ... the price worked for them in the first half," BZW's MacKinnon said.
